justification: Drives the real edit dialog, asserts the refusal names the loop as a sentence rather than a machine code, asserts the dialog stays open, and reads the stored case type back to prove nothing was written.

test_name: a case filed on a child that sets no deadline is due on its parent’s term
justification: Files a case through the New case dialog on a child that declares no deadline and asserts the STORED deadline is exactly the parent's 84 days after the stored start date, so a lost inheritance reddens it.
decisive_assertion: expect(String(stored.deadline ?? '').slice(0, 10), 'the deadline should count the parent’s twelve weeks from the start date').toBe(addDays(startDate, 84))

test_name: a colour and a role picked on the Statuses tab reach the row and a flow
justification: Picks the colour and the role in the real status form, asserts the row swatch carries the orange token and the role cell its label, reads the stored statusType back, and then runs a flow whose step names only the role and asserts the case landed on that status.

test_name: a required checklist item saved on a status becomes a task on the case
justification: Adds and ticks the checklist row in the real form, asserts the row reports one item, asserts the stored checklist equals one required item, then transitions a case into that status and asserts the created task titles equal exactly that item.

test_name: a case filed on a child type is due six weeks after it starts, not twelve
justification: Files a case on the child type through the New case dialog and asserts the STORED deadline is start date plus 42 days, which the parent's twelve weeks would put at 84, so a lost override reddens it.

test_name: admin settings surface renders the Case Type Management heading
justification: Loads the admin settings URL and asserts the Case Type Management section heading renders, so losing the AdminRoot mount reddens it; the Dossiq navigation entry and the ZGW API mapping section the scenario also names go unasserted.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Case Type Management' })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })

test_name: admin settings surface has an add-control for case types
justification: Never establishes the scenario's empty register and asserts neither the empty-state message nor the guidance text, only an add control that renders identically on a populated list.

test_name: the tasks arrive with the status, and show in the Tasks pane
justification: Asserts the case had no tasks for that status beforehand, that both checklist titles exist afterwards, that each row's state is available, and that the Tasks pane on the page shows both.

test_name: an admin's free-form move brings them too
justification: Posts the free-form move, asserts the stored status changed and that both checklist tasks now exist; it reads the task API rather than the Tasks pane the scenario names, so a pane that stopped rendering them would not redden this one.

test_name: back to intake and forward again keeps one set of tasks
justification: Goes back to intake and forward again and asserts exactly two tasks still exist and that the completed one is still completed, which is the de-duplication the requirement states.
decisive_assertion: expect(after, 'a second entry must not double the work').toHaveLength(2)

test_name: the button says which item is still open
justification: Asserts the transition is offered but guardsPassed is false with statusChecklist among the failed guards, that the button is disabled, and that the reason beside it names the open item.

test_name: completing the task frees the case
justification: Asserts guardsPassed flips from false to true on completing the task, that the button is then enabled, and that the move actually lands the case in the target status.

test_name: an optional item does not hold the case
justification: Asserts guardsPassed is true with only the optional item open, that the button is enabled, and that no reason element renders beside it.

test_name: the guard refuses the move posted straight to the API
justification: Asserts the API answers 409 naming statusChecklist and that the case stayed in intake; note the spec now marks this scenario @e2e exclude, saying StatusChecklistGuardTest owns it, so the citation and the exclusion contradict each other and one of the two should go.

test_name: every KPI tile shows a number on the first load of a session
justification: asserts the expected tile count, that every tile's value cell contains a digit rather than a placeholder, and that no Widget not available text appears, which is REQ-DASH-021 exactly
decisive_assertion: await expect(tile.locator('.cn-kpi-card__value'), `the KPI tile "${label}" should show a number, not a placeholder`).toHaveText(/\d/)

test_name: My work lists each of your open tasks once, with days left
justification: asserts each of the three seeded tasks appears exactly once, that the table holds three rows and nothing else, and that the task due tomorrow reads a distance rather than a raw date, so a double-counting table reddens
decisive_assertion: await expect(rows(table), 'My work holds the three seeded tasks and nothing else').toHaveCount(3)

test_name: a My work row opens the task, which is where Pick up and Complete are
justification: the cited scenario now carries an @e2e exclude saying row actions are blocked upstream, and this test contradicts it while asserting only that clicking a My work row navigates to a task URL, never that Complete removes the task from the table or drops the case's task count

test_name: Deadlines holds the overdue and the nearly due, overdue first and in red
justification: asserts the overdue case is on Deadlines exactly once, reads days overdue and carries the danger row class, so the red and presence halves are decisive, but the ordering assertion and the nearly-due row are both behind if guards that let an unlucky fixture pass silently

test_name: a closed case stays off Deadlines, however late it was
justification: requires a Deadlines row to have rendered first, then asserts the closed case is absent from the table and that the four retired tiles are gone, so the absence assertion proves something

test_name: View all on Deadlines opens the Cases list already filtered
justification: asserts the tile is truncated to its row limit, that View all navigates to /cases carrying deadline[lte] and isFinalStatus=false, and that the rendered list excludes the closed and far-future cases after a row has painted, so a dropped filter reddens

test_name: View all on Deadlines opens the Cases list already filtered
justification: the citation names no requirement, only the file; the same test proves the Deadlines tile's View all lands on the Cases list carrying the tile's own deadline window and open-status filter
resolution: no anchor: cites a whole spec file

test_name: View all on Deadlines opens the Cases list already filtered
justification: asserts the View all control exists on the Deadlines tile and navigates to a filtered Cases list, which is the scenario's link clause; the scenario's other clause that the panel shows all overdue cases is not asserted, and the test in fact requires the tile to be truncated

test_name: New case offers the published case type and not the draft
justification: narrows the picker to this run's two types and asserts the published one appears once and the draft zero times, so a picker that stopped filtering drafts reddens
decisive_assertion: await expect(options.filter({ hasText: DRAFT_TYPE }), 'a draft case type must never reach the picker').toHaveCount(0)

test_name: the KPI tiles render numbers on a fresh load, not the widget fallback
justification: Hard-loads the app root in a fresh context and asserts five stat tiles, zero Widget not available fallbacks and a digit in every tile's value, which is the scenario's claim that the tiles each show a number on a first load; it does not check the five tiles by name.

test_name: renders list view with correct controls
justification: Asserts the Cards and Table view toggle, the Add create control and the per-row Actions control on the Cases index, which is three of the scenario's four bullets; only the no Internal Server Error bullet is left unasserted here.

test_name: renders list view with search and filters, and offers no Add
justification: Drives /tasks and asserts the view switcher, that no Add button exists and that the search field is attached, but it never reads a single row, so the scenario's paginated list whose rows show title, parent case reference, status, assignee, due date and priority survives untouched; an empty list passes.

test_name: the Subject column shows the case title, not its uuid
justification: Finds the Subject column by header, asserts no cell holds a raw uuid and then asserts the seeded task's own row shows its case's title in that column, which is the parent case reference the scenario requires of every row.

test_name: renders as a card index scoped to the current user
justification: Asserts the Urgency and Newest sort controls and that a Cards button is visible, but it never switches to Table, never reads the identifier, title, case type, status and deadline columns the scenario names and never asserts card view is the default; note the requirement above the scenario carries an @e2e exclude for being data dependent, which this citation contradicts.

test_name: renders processing time analytics
justification: Asserts the level-2 page heading on /doorlooptijd plus the SLA adherence subtitle and the Dashboard control, so a page that failed to mount reddens; the spec still writes the heading as Processing Time Analytics while the shipped heading, and the assertion, is Processing time.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Processing time', level: 2 })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })

test_name: renders the configuration section and its save control
justification: The in-app /settings page the requirement names was retired, so the test drives /settings/admin/dossiq instead and asserts only that one exact Save button is visible and the body holds no Internal Server Error; none of the three section headings the scenario lists, Version Information, Configuration and Case Type Management, is asserted.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save', exact: true })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })

test_name: admin settings page is accessible to admin users
justification: Loads the admin settings URL, asserts it does not redirect to login and that the Case Type Management heading renders; it does not check the navigation entry or the ZGW mapping section.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Case Type Management' })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })

test_name: a signed-in non-admin is refused the admin settings endpoint with 403
justification: Signs in as the named non-admin, asserts that account holds no admin group and can still read its own settings, then asserts the admin settings URL answers exactly 403 rather than merely not 200.
decisive_assertion: expect(res.status(), `direct URL access to ${ADMIN_SETTINGS_URL} by ${PLAIN_USER} must be 403...`).toBe(403)

test_name: case type list renders its management surface and add control
justification: Its own comment concedes the list body is data-dependent, so it asserts the heading and the add control instead; the empty state message and the guidance sentence the scenario names are never read.

test_name: adding a case type opens the creation view and stores a draft by default
justification: Asserts the New Case Type view opens after clicking Add, and asserts the draft default on the STORED object rather than on a rendered checkbox, which is where that default is actually decided.
decisive_assertion: expect(stored?.isDraft, 'a case type created without an explicit isDraft must be stored as a DRAFT...').toBe(true)

test_name: procest no longer hosts a processing-activities page
justification: Drives the retired route but asserts only that one English heading is absent, never reading the manifest for the navigation entry, the VerwerkingenOverview registration or the integrations gating; the manifest's AvgRegisterLink carries no section key at all, so the scenario's third THEN is already false in the source while this test stays green, and the view file no longer exists so the heading could not render either way.
resolution: cites openspec/changes/**, which gate-19 does not parse

test_name: a case read is logged against a catalogued activity that carries a review status
justification: Walks from a real case read to the stored processing-log entry, asserts it is attributed to the zaakafhandeling catalogue row rather than the unclassified fallback, that the row carries a lifecycle review status, and that the compliance report exposes the unclassified-processing counter, so two of the three capabilities the scenario names redden on a server-side break.
resolution: cites openspec/changes/**, which gate-19 does not parse
decisive_assertion: expect(['concept', 'published', 'archived'], `the catalogue row carries a review status, got ...`).toContain(attributed?.status)

test_name: the inzageverzoek export returns the logged read of that data subject
justification: Reads a seeded role and then polls the per betrokkene inzage export until it lists that read, and asserts the subject block, the count, the actor, that every returned read belongs to that subject and that a bare call is refused with 400, so an export that answers empty for everyone reddens.
resolution: cites openspec/changes/**, which gate-19 does not parse
decisive_assertion: await expect.poll(async () => { ... return reads.map((r) => r.objectUuid) }, { timeout: 15_000, ... }).toContain(roleUuid)

test_name: start-case flow offers Person / Company / Contact and stays skippable
justification: Asserts all three initiator types are offered and that the step stays skippable with the confirm disabled and Skip enabled, so removing the Contact type or making a pick mandatory reddens it; it drives the StartCaseWidget step rather than the Dashboard New case form the scenario names.

test_name: person search lists a seeded personen-mock persona with BSN
justification: Searches by surname and asserts the matching result row carries the persona's BSN and birthdate, which is exactly the scenario's name, birthdate and BSN clause; a picker that listed names only would fail.

test_name: company search by pinned KvK number lists the fixture company
justification: Searches the pinned KvK number and asserts the fixture company row is listed with that number, so a Company search that stopped reaching kvkCompany or dropped the number from the result line reddens.

test_name: contact tab shows an explicit empty state, never an error toast
justification: Drives the Contact tab and asserts the empty state plus the absence of any error toast, but it never establishes the scenario's GIVEN: /contactsmenu/contacts is core and answers 200 with no matches on the runner, so deleting the try/catch in searchContacts that implements the degrade would not redden this test.

test_name: picked persona persists as projection and shows on case detail with source link
justification: Reads the stored case back through the API and asserts requester resolves to the brpPerson row with that BSN and that all three projection fields hold the persona's values, which is the stored-state assertion the scenario asks for rather than an HTTP echo.

test_name: picked persona persists as projection and shows on case detail with source link
justification: Asserts the case detail card shows the name, the type Person and the BSN rendered as a link whose href resolves to the requester's own contact page, so dropping the source link or the card reddens it.

test_name: a case created without initiator renders no initiator block
justification: Creates a case through Skip and asserts both halves: the stored row carries no requester and no projection, and the rendered page shows the initiator-empty cell with no initiator-section, against a tab strip first proven visible so an absent card is a decision rather than a pending render.

test_name: shared-mailbox settings render without per-user SMTP send fields
justification: Loads every admin section, proves the shared-mailbox section actually rendered via its heading and the IMAP host input, then asserts no input carries smtp in its id or name, so the negative cannot pass on an unrendered page.

test_name: the case list shows a sub-case badge, and only on a parent
justification: Seeds its own parent with one sub-case and asserts the badge is visible on that row in either locale spelling, so a badge that stopped rendering or resolved to no count reddens it.
decisive_assertion: await expect(withChild.getByText(BADGE).first(), 'a case with one sub-case shows the sub-case badge').toBeVisible({ timeout: 60_000 })

test_name: the case list shows a sub-case badge, and only on a parent
justification: Seeds a second parent with no children, asserts that row is visible first so absence is claimed next to presence, then asserts the badge pattern has zero matches inside it.
decisive_assertion: await expect(withoutChild.getByText(BADGE), 'a case with no sub-cases shows no badge').toHaveCount(0)

test_name: the case list shows a sub-case badge, and only on a parent
justification: Counts requests to /api/deelzaken/counts and allows up to two, but the list is narrowed by title to a single seeded row, so a per-row N+1 implementation also makes one request and passes; widen the fixture to several parents on one page to make the batching claim falsifiable.
decisive_assertion: expect(countCalls.length, `deelzaken counts must be batched per page, saw ${countCalls.length} requests`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2)

test_name: the sub-cases page warns about orphans for a parent with sub-cases
justification: Seeds a parent with a child, opens the sub-cases page and asserts unconditionally that the orphan dialog title and its unlink sentence appear; it cancels rather than confirming, so the scenario's nulling-of-parentCase clauses are proved by the sibling test at line 929, not here.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByText('Delete case with sub-cases').first(), 'a parent with sub-cases takes the orphan-warning branch, not the plain confirm').toBeVisi...

test_name: the sub-cases page warns about orphans for a parent with sub-cases
justification: This test seeds a parent WITH a sub-case and only ever exercises the orphan branch, so nothing in it says what a childless case's delete dialog looks like; breaking the plain confirmation would leave every assertion here green, and the honest citation for this scenario is the sibling test at line 400.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByText(/unlink the sub-cases from their parent/i).first()).toBeVisible()

test_name: a parent with no sub-cases takes the plain delete confirmation
justification: Seeds a parent with no children and asserts both sides: the standard confirmation copy is visible and the orphan sentence has zero matches, so a build that warned about orphans on every delete reddens it.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByText('Are you sure you want to delete this case?').first()).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 })

test_name: the Sub-cases tab renders either a list or an empty state without error
justification: The helper does assert the sub-cases section renders something, but the test's own assertion is expect(hasTable || hasEmpty).toBeTruthy(), which an empty state satisfies, and it opens whatever case the register hands back first, so the scenario's three sub-cases with title, status, assignee, deadline and clickable links are never read.

test_name: the Sub-cases tab renders either a list or an empty state without error
justification: Same or-disjunction: hasTable satisfies it, so the empty-state sentence the scenario names need never render, and the Create Sub-case button the scenario also requires is not asserted at all; the fixture is an arbitrary existing case that may well have sub-cases.

test_name: opening a sub-case shows the parent breadcrumb and the list shows a completion roll-up
justification: The breadcrumb assertion sits inside if ((await breadcrumb.count()) > 0) with an else branch that writes an annotation and passes, and the row click is wrapped in .catch(() => {}), so a case detail that renders no parent breadcrumb at all reports green.

test_name: opening a sub-case shows the parent breadcrumb and the list shows a completion roll-up
justification: Nothing in this test opens a case with a null parentCase or asserts the absence of a breadcrumb on one; the only unconditional assertions it leaves for this scenario are that the section rendered and that the body does not read Internal Server Error.

test_name: opening a sub-case shows the parent breadcrumb and the list shows a completion roll-up
justification: The roll-up assertion is guarded by if ((await rollup.count()) > 0), so a header that prints no roll-up passes, and even inside the guard it matches any X/Y rather than the counts the seeded fixture would imply; no sub-case is given an endDate anywhere in the test.

test_name: opening a sub-case shows the parent breadcrumb and the list shows a completion roll-up
justification: Same guarded roll-up locator and the same any-X-over-Y pattern; the scenario's specific 0/2 case is never seeded and the zero-completed reading is never distinguished from the completed one.

test_name: an eligible parent offers Create sub-case, filtered to its own subCaseTypes, and the created case carries parentCase
justification: Seeds a parent whose type allows exactly two child types, asserts the dropdown offers exactly those two and not the stranger type, and then reads the created case back from the register to pin parentCase and caseType.

test_name: a parent whose case type allows no sub-case types is refused server-side and offers no Create control
justification: Asserts the server refuses with 409 and the reason case_type_not_allowed, then that the page offers zero Create controls and says why, so a build that only hid the button reddens on the API half.

test_name: a closed parent is refused server-side and offers no Create control
justification: Asserts a 409 with reason parent_closed, proves the same child type still validates on the open twin so the refusal is attributable to the endDate alone, and asserts zero Create controls beside the page's own explanation.

test_name: a case that is itself a sub-case is refused server-side and offers no Create control
justification: Reads the fixture back to confirm it really carries a parentCase, asserts a 409 with reason grandparenting_forbidden, and asserts zero Create controls next to the page's stated reason.

test_name: deleting a parent with sub-cases warns about the orphans and nulls parentCase on every child
justification: Seeds a parent with exactly two children, asserts both rows are on the page, asserts the orphan warning unconditionally, confirms the delete and then polls the STORED children to prove parentCase was cleared rather than left dangling.
decisive_assertion: expect(child.parentCase ?? null, `case ${childId} must be unlinked, not left pointing at a deleted parent`).toBeFalsy()

test_name: deleting a case with no sub-cases takes the plain confirmation, with no orphan warning
justification: Seeds a childless case, asserts the empty state exactly, asserts the standard confirmation copy is visible and that the orphan warning has zero matches, so the pair discriminates the two branches rather than smoke-testing both.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByText(/Are you sure you want to delete this case/i)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15_000 })

test_name: cases index renders so a case dossier tab can be opened
justification: Asserts only that /cases does not print Internal Server Error, and never opens a dossier tab, so the type grouping and the Dossier (8) count badge the requirement specifies go unobserved.

test_name: cases index renders so a case dossier tab can be opened
justification: Same body as the row above: a 500-string check on the cases index, with no empty dossier opened and no assertion on the upload call to action or the drag and drop zone.

test_name: dossier sort and per-file progress are not observable here, blocked by #764
justification: The body opens with an unconditional test.fixme(true, ...), so nothing runs and the citation claims per-column sort and filter coverage that is never executed; the fixme reason states this plainly.
decisive_assertion: test.fixme(true, '#764: REQ-ZAK-004c (per-column sort and filter with URL state) and REQ-ZAK-005b ... have no assertion in this suite ...')

test_name: dossier sort and per-file progress are not observable here, blocked by #764
justification: Unconditional test.fixme(true, ...): per-file upload progress is never observed, and the only statement after it is a 500-string check on the cases index.
decisive_assertion: test.fixme(true, '#764: ... REQ-ZAK-005b (per-file progress read mid-upload) have no assertion in this suite ...')

test_name: version history needs a multi-version document, blocked by #764
justification: Unconditional test.fixme(true, ...) because no seeded document carries a second Nextcloud file version, so no version list and no restore control is ever asserted.
decisive_assertion: test.fixme(true, '#764: REQ-ZAK-006a needs an informatieobject carrying more than one Nextcloud file version ...')

test_name: ZIP export contents are not asserted in the browser, blocked by #764
justification: Unconditional test.fixme(true, ...): the ZIP is never downloaded or unpacked, so manifest.csv and the per-type sub-folders are asserted only in Newman and ZipManifestBuilderTest, not here.
decisive_assertion: test.fixme(true, '#764: REQ-ZAK-008a needs the downloaded ZIP unpacked to assert manifest.csv and the per-type sub-folders ...')

test_name: an executable is refused before storage, by extension and by magic bytes alike
justification: Both halves of the requirement are driven with a control first: a plain PDF must not be screened as an executable, then malware.exe and an MZ-headered besluit.pdf each come back 422 with the filename and the reason, and the register is read to prove neither row was ever stored.
decisive_assertion: expect(ours, `${name} must never reach the register`).toHaveLength(0)

test_name: the metadata dialog lists every selected file and issues no upload while required fields are empty
justification: Asserts the dialog lists both filenames, that the Upload button exists and is disabled, that a forced click neither closes it nor sends anything, and then that filling the type releases exactly two posts carrying the one shared informatieobjecttype.
decisive_assertion: expect(uploads, 'no upload may be sent while the dialog is still incomplete').toBe(0)

test_name: a bulk status transition answers per document, and the register agrees with every verdict
justification: Sends a deliberately mixed batch and asserts a per-id verdict for each document, with the archived one refused by name and reason, then reads each stored row back so a result list that reports one thing and writes another reddens.
decisive_assertion: expect(String(stored.status), `the stored status of ${id} must match the verdict the bulk call reported for it`).toBe(expected)

test_name: renders the processing time page heading on navigation
justification: asserts only that a level-2 heading reading Processing time is visible and that the body carries no Internal Server Error, and the scenario names the heading Processing Time Analytics, which the page no longer renders, so the spec text is stale and the test proves only that the page loaded
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: HEADING, level: 2 })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 15000 })

test_name: shows empty state when no case data is available
justification: fulfils the case collection read with an empty list, asserts the no-case-data empty state is visible, and asserts the intercept actually answered, so an empty state reached by a failed fetch or an unread endpoint cannot pass it
decisive_assertion: expect(emptyAnswers, 'The empty state must come from the empty case list served for ...').toBeGreaterThan(0)

test_name: the cases-on-map view renders its filter sidebar and counts the located cases
justification: Asserts both sidebar comboboxes by accessible name and pins the count summary to an exact string against a fixed three-row mock of which two carry geometry, so a view that placed the geometry-less case or lost the summary reddens.

test_name: an unreachable case backend surfaces a notice instead of a broken page
justification: Aborts the case read and asserts the exact notice text plus a sidebar and map that are still there, which is the scenario's degrade-gracefully clause, but it only covers a network abort: the file's own comment records that a 500 with a JSON body raises no notice today.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.locator('.cases-on-map__notice')).toContainText('Map data could not be loaded. Showing what is available.', ...)

test_name: substitution renders under personal settings with a register action
justification: Asserts the personal settings mount point and a Register substitution button render, never submitting a registration, so nothing about the created object's absentee, substitute, status or createdBy is checked.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /Register substitution|Waarneming registreren/i }).first(), 'the Vue app mounted...').toBeVisible(...)

test_name: a substitution naming one user as both absentee and substitute is refused, and writes nothing
justification: Posts a self-substitution, asserts the 400 and an error naming the rule, and then asserts on the store that no row carrying the probe marker was written and that the substitution count is unchanged.
decisive_assertion: expect(after.filter((row) => String(row?.comment ?? '') === marker), 'the rejected submission must not have left a substitution behind').toHaveLength(0)

test_name: a signed-in user without the coordinator role is refused both reassignment endpoints
justification: Probes both reassignment endpoints as a named non-admin account, asserts 403 on each, asserts no case was transferred, and runs the same preview as the coordinator as a control so a route broken for everyone cannot pass as a working guard.
decisive_assertion: expect(preview.status(), `the reassignment PREVIEW must be denied to a non-coordinator; body was ...`).toBe(403)

test_name: the coordinator preview lists the departing handler open work and mutates nothing
justification: Runs the preview and asserts both open cases come back with title, case type and a status key plus a tasks array, then asserts @self.updated is unchanged on both cases so a preview that quietly re-saved a row reddens.
decisive_assertion: expect(afterIn?.['@self']?.updated, 'the preview must not have written to the case it previewed').toBe(beforeIn?.['@self']?.updated)

test_name: My Work renders without error and supports the substituted filter when present
justification: Asserts only that the My Work page renders an Urgency button and no Internal Server Error text, and the substituted toggle is clicked inside an if that simply skips when the toggle is absent, so a build routing no substituted work at all stays green.

test_name: a caseTypes-scoped substitution routes the covered type and withholds the rest
justification: Reads /api/substitutions/work and asserts the covered case type reaches the waarnemer while the case of the uncovered type does not, which is exactly the MUST NOT half of the scope limit.
decisive_assertion: expect(routed, 'a case of a type OUTSIDE the substitution scope must never reach the waarnemer').not.toContain(outOfScopeCaseId)

test_name: every capacity-stamped action under a substitution is returned, in chronological order
justification: Asserts the actions endpoint returns both seeded entries oldest first, each naming actor, absentee and case title, so a missing sort or a dropped entry reddens; the entries are seeded by hand, so the stamping half is knowingly unclaimed.
decisive_assertion: expect(mine.map((entry) => String(entry?.action ?? '')), 'both stamped actions must come back, oldest first ...').toEqual([STAMPED_EARLIER, STAMPED_LATER])

test_name: coordinator admin exposes a bulk-reassign action with a mandatory preview
justification: Asserts the coordinator console offers Bulk reassign and a Preview affected work button, which is a different requirement from registering a substitution on behalf of an absent handler, and the whole body sits behind a becomesVisible guard that skips the test when the heading does not appear.
decisive_assertion: await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /Preview affected work/ }).first()).toBeVisible({ timeout: 8000 })

test_name: no sidebar link points into another app
justification: Points at openspec/specs/avg-processing-surface/spec.md, which does not exist; the identical anchor does resolve inside the open change at openspec/changes/page-topology-cleanup/specs/avg-processing-surface/spec.md, and the nearest published capability is avg-verwerkingenlogging.
resolution: the cited spec file does not exist
